findings.title: No branch protection on default branch
findings.description: The default branch 'main' has no branch protection rules.
findings.remediation: Enable branch protection rules: require PR reviews, status checks, restrict force pushes.
findings.reasoning: FAIL: The default branch 'main' on Jriley711/iso27001-dashboard has NO branch protection rules configured. This means: (1) Anyone with write access can push directly to the main branch without review. (2) Code changes bypass all quality gates and peer review. (3) Force pushes can rewrite history and destroy audit trails. (4) The branch can be deleted. This is a fundamental change management failure. SOC 2 CC8.1 requires that changes are authorized, tested, and approved before implementation. ISO 27001 A.12.1.2 requires documented change management procedures. Without branch protection, there is no enforced separation of duties between code author and code reviewer.

findings.title: Missing security policy
findings.remediation: Add a SECURITY.md file with vulnerability reporting instructions.
findings.reasoning: FAIL: Repository Jriley711/iso27001-dashboard has no SECURITY.md file. Without a security policy, external researchers or users who discover vulnerabilities have no documented way to report them responsibly. This increases the risk of public disclosure without a fix (zero-day). SOC 2 CC1.1 requires governance documentation. CC7.4 requires incident response processes. ISO 27001 A.16.1.2 requires mechanisms for reporting security events.

findings.title: Missing .gitignore
findings.description: No .gitignore file. Sensitive files may be accidentally committed.
findings.remediation: Add a .gitignore file appropriate for your tech stack.
findings.reasoning: WARNING: Repository Jriley711/iso27001-dashboard has no .gitignore file. Without it, developers may accidentally commit sensitive files such as .env (credentials), private keys, or build artifacts. SOC 2 CC6.1 requires access controls over sensitive information. ISO 27001 A.9.4.1 requires information access restriction.

findings.title: No sensitive environment files committed
findings.description: No .env, .env.local, or .env.production files found in repository.
findings.reasoning: PASS: Repository Jriley711/iso27001-dashboard does not have any common environment files (.env, .env.local, .env.production) committed. Secrets appear to be managed outside of version control, which is the expected practice per SOC 2 CC6.1 and ISO 27001 A.9.4.1.

findings.title: Dependabot not configured
findings.remediation: Add .github/dependabot.yml to enable automated security updates.
findings.reasoning: WARNING: Repository Jriley711/iso27001-dashboard does not have Dependabot configured. Without automated dependency scanning, the project may unknowingly use libraries with known critical vulnerabilities (CVEs). For example, a vulnerable version of a logging library (like Log4Shell) could remain in the codebase indefinitely. SOC 2 CC7.1 requires ongoing vulnerability identification and remediation. ISO 27001 A.12.6.1 requires timely management of technical vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Missing LICENSE file
findings.remediation: Add a LICENSE file (MIT, Apache 2.0, etc.) to define usage terms.
findings.reasoning: WARNING: Repository Jriley711/iso27001-dashboard has no LICENSE file. Without a license, the code is technically under exclusive copyright by default — others cannot legally use, modify, or distribute it. For open-source projects, this creates legal ambiguity.
